content: Leonotis leonurus, commonly referred to as Wild Dagga or Lion's Tail, is a plant species belonging to the genus Leonotis within the Lamiaceae family, which is also known as the mint family. This plant is indigenous to the southern regions of Africa. Within the genus Leonotis, there are approximately thirty species of plants classified under the Lamiaceae family. However, only one other species, Leonotis nepetifolia (commonly known as Klip Dagga), shares the entheogenic properties of Leonotis leonurus. A distinguishing feature between these two species is that the flowers of Leonotis nepetifolia emerge from a spherical, spiny structure. Leonotis species have been utilized in traditional medicine to address a variety of health conditions. These include epilepsy, diabetes, insect bites and stings, skin disorders, muscular cramps, respiratory ailments, hypertension, headaches, viral hepatitis, intestinal parasitic infections, obesity, and eczema. Notably, in 1992, Wild Dagga was demonstrated to reduce breast tumor growth in mice. The most common method of preparation involves harvesting the leaves, drying them, and brewing them into a tea. The plant contains a chemical compound known as leonurine, which functions as a mild vasodilator and a smooth muscle relaxant.
